result.title: Probabilistic Steering of Generative Priors for Lab-in-the-Loop Antibody Optimization
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS `26 GEM and NeurIPS `26 AI4DD
result.summary: Therapeutic antibody development is often framed as comprising two discrete stages: initial discovery of novel binders followed by iterative optimization to refine these hits into therapeutic-grade molecules. Models and methods often reflect these stages, with generative structure models applied to discovery and probabilistic black-box optimization methods applied to refinement. Here we propose to unify these stages by smoothly transitioning a generative discovery model into iterative optimization, allowing the handoff between the structure-based prior and supervision from wet lab data to be guided by the posterior uncertainty of a probabilistic surrogate. We show that this yields improvements in optimization efficiency in the low-N regime, as well as improved diversity amongst the optimized molecules.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将基于结构的生成式抗体发现模型平滑过渡到湿实验闭环优化，用概率代理模型的后验不确定性引导结构先验与实验监督之间的交接，在低样本条件下提升优化效率与分子多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以「后验不确定性」门控先验与外部证据之间切换的机制，可能可供核查为 LVR 中 STOP/证据筛选的信号设计线索，即何时停止依赖 latent 先验、转向新观测；但任务领域与视觉推理差异较大，仅属概念性启发。
